definition: the framework of bones that supports a body
hook: Skeleton was never the word for bones. It was the word for what is left.
modernAnchor: A plastic one on a porch, a real one in a museum. We call it a skeleton.
journey: Greek skellein meant to dry up or parch, the verb you would use for a field in a drought.
Greeks used skeletos for a body dried out by sun and time, a mummy or a withered corpse.
The word named the whole dried body, flesh and all, not just the bones inside it.
Latin and then English narrowed it over the centuries until only the bones kept the name.
